question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Mughal Farmans/Privileges granted to English — location of issuance]
options: Surat — English factory permitted under Mughal farman after English naval victories (1612–13)
Agra — Site where Emperor Jahangir issued early informal assurances of trade protection to English merchants
Hooghly — English factory in Bengal established with Mughal permission under Shah Jahan's farman
Madras — English received Mughal farman authorising their Fort St. George settlement in 1639
wrong_fact: Madras (Fort St. George, 1639) was established on land granted by the local Nayak ruler of Chandragiri (a Telugu chieftain), NOT by Mughal farman. Madras was outside Mughal territorial control, being in the Deccan/South India.
explanation: Surat factory (post-1612) and Agra assurances were within Mughal territory. Hooghly in Bengal was under Mughal suzerainty and needed Mughal permission. But Fort St. George, Madras was built on land leased from the Nayak of Chandragiri — the Mughals had no jurisdiction there.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Mughal Farmans granting English privileges — emperor and region]
options: Jahangir — Granted informal assurances of trade at Surat and other western ports after 1613
Shah Jahan — Issued farman permitting English factory at Hooghly (Bengal) after their assistance during Mughal-Portuguese hostilities
Aurangzeb — Issued farman restoring English trading rights after the Child's War (1690), permitting re-entry at Surat
Akbar — Issued the first Mughal farman formally granting English East India Company exclusive trade rights at Broach
wrong_fact: Akbar never issued a farman to the English East India Company — the EIC was founded in 1600, right at the end of Akbar's reign, and made no significant contact with Akbar. There was certainly no farman granting exclusive rights at Broach.
explanation: Jahangir's era saw the first meaningful English-Mughal contacts (Hawkins, Roe). Shah Jahan permitted English at Hooghly. Aurangzeb's farman after Child's War (1690) restored English trade. Akbar had no substantive dealings with the EIC, and the 'Broach exclusive farman' is entirely fictitious.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Mughal Farmans — specific rights granted in specific locations]
options: Surat — Farman permitted English to trade duty-free (nishan) in Gujarat after 1612 naval victories
Hooghly/Bengal — English permitted to trade on payment of customs in Bengal under Shah Jahan (c.1651 farman)
Masulipatnam — English factory established 1611 under farman from Golconda Sultan, not Mughal emperor
Bombay — Mughal farman of Aurangzeb assigned Bombay island to the English as a strategic base in 1668
wrong_fact: Bombay was ceded to England as part of Catherine of Braganza's dowry (Portuguese princess) when she married King Charles II in 1661, then leased to the EIC in 1668. It was a Portuguese-British transaction, not a Mughal farman.
explanation: Surat trading rights emerged post-1612. Bengal trade under Shah Jahan is historically accurate. Masulipatnam indeed fell under Golconda's jurisdiction. However, Bombay's transfer to English control was a Portuguese dowry arrangement (1661), not a Mughal imperial farman — the Mughals had no say in this.
